title: The city of Brahman in the heart
hookLine: inside the body is a small lotus-shaped house, and inside that a small space, as big as all the space outside
carry: Brahman dwells in the space in the heart
tomorrow: Indra and Virochana learn from Prajapati

lines: A CITY, A HOUSE, A ROOM.
cards: Russian nesting dolls get smaller as you go in. Open the big one, and there's a smaller one; open that, smaller again, until a tiny solid doll the size of a bean.
The last chapter of the Chandogya opens with a nesting picture too: a city, a house, a room. Only this one does the opposite. The farther in you go, the bigger it gets.

teach.h: THE CITY, THE LOTUS, THE SMALL SPACE.
teach.b: In this city of Brahman, the eighth chapter begins, there is a small house shaped like a lotus, and inside it a small space. What is inside that space should be sought, and understood. The city of Brahman is the body.
The lotus-shaped house is the heart. And the small space is, well, small. So the students ask the obvious question.
A tiny space in a tiny house in this body: what could be in there worth looking for?

teach.h: AS LARGE AS ALL THE SPACE OUTSIDE.
teach.b: The teacher answers: as large as this space out here is, that large is the space within the heart. Both heaven and earth are contained in it. Fire and wind, sun and moon, lightning and stars.
Whatever there is here, and whatever there isn't, all of it is held there. The students push again, and it's a good question.

teach.h: IT DOESN'T AGE WHEN THE BODY AGES.
teach.b: If everything is held inside this body, what's left when the body grows old, or dies? The answer: that doesn't grow old when the body grows old. It isn't killed when the body is killed.
That is the real city of Brahman. And the text describes that inner self: free from evil, from old age, from death, from grief, from hunger and thirst. Its desires are true.

teach.h: THE LORD DWELLS IN THE HEART OF ALL BEINGS.
teach.b: Here the same word as the honest boy's name, satyakama, describes the self in every heart.
So the nesting dolls run backward: body, heart, a small space, and inside it, everything. This is the Hindu teaching that God isn't only out there.
The Gita says the Lord dwells in the heart of all beings, and many devotees picture God seated in the lotus of the heart when they pray.

how: Meditation on the space in the heart, the dahara-vidya, is taught in several Hindu traditions, and many devotional schools picture God dwelling in the lotus of the heart.

o: the lotus seat where a god is enthroned
a cave where sages go to meditate alone
small and subtle: the space within the heart

games.q: the nesting picture — tap the pairs.
p: as large as all space outside

s: the small space in the heart is tiny inside, too
as large as all the space outside, holding heaven and earth.
the text says the inner self doesn't age when the body ages
it isn't killed when the body is killed.
the word satyakama appears here describing the self
the boy's name from chapter four, now a quality of the self in every heart.

games.q: you're a student. your teacher says there's a small space in your heart worth seeking. you ask what could be in something so small. what's the answer?
o: as large as all space outside: heaven and earth, sun and moon.
games.why: the space in the heart is as large as the space outside. heaven, earth, fire, wind, sun, moon, lightning and stars are all held in it.

practice: Breathe into the center of your chest and imagine a small, quiet space there, like a closed lotus. If you pray, picture the form of God you love seated inside it; if you don't, a small steady light.
On each breath out, let the lotus open, wider than your chest, wider than the room, as wide as the sky.

wordCard.voice: Dahara, small, subtle. The body is the city, the heart a lotus-shaped house, and the small space inside holds heaven and earth.

orig.note: Sanskrit dahara: small, subtle. the daharākāśa, the small space in the heart.

carryVoice: Your line: Brahman dwells in the space in the heart. Heaven and earth, held in a space that small. Day three hundred fifty-six.

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 8.1.1–6 (the city of Brahman; the lotus; the small space; free from old age and death)
Bhagavad Gita 18.61 (the Lord dwells in the heart of all beings)
